subject: Close sequencing & dependency plan for MSA/DPA/order form - GreenPath Health
messages:
From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@greenpathhealth.com>
To: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Cc: procurement@greenpathhealth.com
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 09:14:00 -0800
Subject: Kickoff: close sequencing and evaluation MAP

Hi Lukas,

Thanks again for the demo last week — the team here at GreenPath liked the latency numbers and the model rollback story. Procurement asked me to send you a short note with timing constraints so we can map dependencies up front. High level:

- Our SOC 2 and security review for vendors finishes the week of Mar 22 (audit report expected Mar 24).
- Procurement would like an executed MSA + Order Form by Mar 31 if possible to hit our Q2 integration window.
- We need a signed DPA before any production data is sent to Redwood (legal insists).

Can you share a mutual action plan that shows: 1) the document sequencing (MSA/DPA/Order Form), 2) estimated internal legal review times, and 3) outcomes that would unblock an integration pilot?

I've attached our preferred procurement checklist and a high-level SOW sample. If you want, procurement can join a short call to align on signatory order.

Thanks,
Sarah Park
Director, Vendor Programs
GreenPath Health

Attachments: GreenPath_Procurement_Checklist.pdf (pdf), SOW_sample.docx (docx)

From: Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
To: Sarah Park <sarah.park@greenpathhealth.com>
Cc: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 1 Mar 2027 12:03:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: close sequencing and evaluation MAP

Sarah — thanks for the clear constraints. I've sketched a recommended sequencing below and attached a draft MAP and a dependency grid for your procurement/legal team to review. Short summary:

1) NDA / preliminary data access agreement (if needed) — optional; can be parallel to security questionnaire.
2) DPA signed before production data is exchanged (we can accept a redline but prefer to use Redwood standard DPA + appendix).
3) MSA review and redlines — typical turnaround 5–7 business days from receipt for standard enterprise edits; longer if unusual indemnity or data residency clauses are introduced.
4) Order Form (pricing and billing) — executed last (sign off after MSA + DPA accepted).

Proposed timeline to meet your Mar 31 ask: we need GreenPath to return any MSA redlines by Mar 10 so Legal can triage and respond by Mar 18. DPA should be provided with the first pass of MSA so we can bundle negotiation. If GreenPath procurement can accept our standard SOC attestation language (we'll share the SOC 2 summary), that should shorten the path.

Action items for your side:
- Procurement: confirm preferred signatory order (procurement -> legal -> finance)
- Legal: send initial MSA + DPA redlines to marissa_cole@redwood.com by Mar 10
- Security: confirm whether the SOC 2 report will be sufficient or if you require a bridge letter (due Mar 24)

We can run a 30-min MAP review with procurement this week — Neha will be the Redwood PM for the pilot and will own the milestone checklist.

Best,
Lukas Meyer
Principal Sales Engineer
Redwood Inference

Attachments: MAP_GreenPath_v0.1.xlsx (xlsx), MSA_DPA_dependency_matrix.pdf (pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Internal: GreenPath sequencing — quick legal triage request

Team — forwarding the procurement constraints from GreenPath. Key points I want legal to sign off on before we present the MAP to the customer:

- Order of signatures: GreenPath prefers procurement first, then legal, then finance. Is that okay operationally?
- DPA: customer will push their template; we should identify 3 "deal-breaker" clauses we will not accept and mark negotiable items.
- SOC 2: timeline suggests we won't be able to supply the final report until after their audit completes; confirm whether a SOC 2 summary + control attest letter is acceptable to GreenPath (they said they might accept).

If Jonas can review the attached dependency matrix and add a short FAQ for procurement (how to sequence sign-off, typical turnaround lengths, and expedite path), that would be ideal. Happy to run a short sync if needed.

Marissa
Head of Enterprise Sales Ops
Redwood Inference

Quoted: "On Mon, 1 Mar 2027 12:03:00 -0700, Lukas Meyer wrote:
> Proposed timeline to meet your Mar 31 ask: we need GreenPath to return any MSA redlines by Mar 10...

Attachments for legal: MSA_DPA_dependency_matrix.pdf (pdf)"

From: Jonas Weber <jonas_weber@redwood.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>, Neha Kapoor <neha_kapoor@redwood.com>, Lukas Meyer <lukas_meyer@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 3 Mar 2027 11:47:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Internal: GreenPath sequencing — quick legal triage request

Marissa / team — reviewed the matrix and put our recommended fast-track plan inline below. High level: we can meet the proposed timeline if GreenPath returns redlines quickly and agrees to a few constraints.

Top-level legal guidance (fast-track):
- Accept procurement-first signatory order; Redwood will countersign the Order Form last.
- DPA: we can accept GreenPath's template with 3 non-negotiable constraints: (1) max liability stays as negotiated in the MSA, (2) no additional data resale rights, (3) security incident notification timelines at or below 72 hours. Everything else negotiable.
- If GreenPath wants a major indemnity change or data localization obligations beyond our standard policy, that will add 7–10 business days.

Triage path:
1) GreenPath sends marked MSA + DPA by Mar 10 (we'll assign a primary reviewer).
2) Legal issues triaged within 48 hours; high-impact items escalated to our GC for decision.
3) Target Redwood response to customer redlines by Mar 18.

If we see anything materially new in their MSA/DPA, we'll flag an internal "expedite" call. I can also draft a 1-page procurement FAQ for Marissa to send to GreenPath procurement that explains the signatory order and turnaround SLAs.

Jonas Weber
Senior Counsel, Contracts
Redwood Inference

Quoted: "On Tue, 2 Mar 2027 09:02:00 -0700, Marissa Cole wrote:
> If Jonas can review the attached dependency matrix and add a short FAQ...
"

From: Sarah Park <sarah.park@greenpathhealth.com>

Cc: procurement@greenpathhealth.com
Date: Mon, 15 Mar 2027 16:20:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Kickoff: close sequencing and evaluation MAP

Hi Lukas / Marissa — apologies for the delayed note. Procurement and legal have reviewed the MAP and dependency grid. A few quick items to confirm before we move to signatures:

- GreenPath confirms signatory order: procurement -> legal -> finance (ok to countersign Order Form last).
- We accept the 3 DPA constraints you noted (liability cap alignment, no resale, 72hr incident notification).
- GreenPath will return a single consolidated redline document for MSA + DPA by EOD Mar 18.

Attached: MAP_GreenPath_v1.xlsx (finalized milestones), MSA_DPA_dependency_matrix.pdf (annotated). Procurement also shared the DocuSign envelope for the Order Form; link below.

Next steps:
- Mar 18: GreenPath submits consolidated redlines
- Mar 19–23: Redwood legal triage and respond
- Mar 24–29: Final signoffs and DocuSign circulation

If this stays on track we will hit the Mar 31 execution target. Thanks for the clear runbook and for offering the procurement FAQ — that will help our SMEs run the internal approval.

Regards,
Sarah Park
Director, Vendor Programs
GreenPath Health
